name: InferenceNetwork

methods.name: setSettings
methods.desc:
Replaces the settings. The settle window stays between 5 minutes and 7 days, and the unbonding
delay between 14 days and a year, so a provider that overcharged and then leaves can still be
slashed once it is caught. Open tickets keep the expiry they opened with.

methods.name: setPaymentAsset
methods.desc:
Accepts or stops accepting `asset` for new tickets. The first call for an asset creates its box, paid by
`payment` (INFERENCE_ASSET_MBR); later calls take a zero payment.

methods.name: setProviderStatus
methods.desc: Activates a Pending or Paused provider, or pauses a Pending or Active one. A paused provider takes no new tickets but can settle open ones.

methods.name: slash
methods.desc: Takes up to the provider's whole bond and sends it to `receiver`.

methods.name: optIn
methods.desc: Opts this app in to `asset`; `payment` covers the opt-in minimum balance.

methods.name: sweepFees
methods.desc: Sends the fees accrued in `asset` to the treasury.

methods.name: registerProvider
methods.desc:
Registers the sender as a provider's owner. `payment` pays for the provider and metadata boxes
(providerCost); `bond` transfers at least the DAO's provider bond in AKTA. While registration is
closed the provider starts Pending until the admin activates it.

methods.name: setMetadata
methods.desc:
Replaces the metadata URI. `payment` pays the new box in full (metadataCost) and the old box's
deposit goes back to the owner.

methods.name: setAttestation
methods.desc: Publishes or replaces the provider's attestation. The first one takes INFERENCE_ATTESTATION_MBR, later ones zero.

methods.name: addBond
methods.desc: Adds to a provider's bond, in its bond asset. Anyone may add.

methods.name: beginUnbond
methods.desc: Starts leaving the network: no new tickets (open ones can still be settled), and the bond can be withdrawn after the unbonding delay.

methods.name: withdrawBond
methods.desc: After the unbonding delay, returns what is left of the bond to the owner.

methods.name: open
methods.desc:
Opens a ticket for one request: `payment` pays the ticket box (INFERENCE_TICKET_MBR), `lock`
moves the request's max price in `asset` from the sender (the payer) to this app, and `request` is
the caller's id for the request, which the provider sees in the same request. The ticket must be
settled before the settle window ends, or anyone can refund it. Returns the ticket id.

Providers serve without waiting for this to confirm: a provider whose ticket never lands cuts the
payer off, losing at most that request.

args.name: request
args.desc: The caller's id for the request, so the provider can match the ticket to what it served.

methods.name: createPool
methods.desc:
Creates a sponsor pool in `asset`, owned by the sender. `payment` pays the pool box
(INFERENCE_POOL_MBR) and anything above it becomes the pool's credit for ticket and usage boxes.
Fund it with `fundPool`. Returns the pool id.

methods.name: fundPool
methods.desc: Adds to a pool's balance, in its asset. Anyone may fund a pool.

methods.name: addPoolCredit
methods.desc: Adds ALGO to a pool's credit for ticket and usage boxes. Anyone may add.

methods.name: updatePool
methods.desc: The sponsor changes who may open pool tickets and how much each member gets.

methods.name: withdrawPool
methods.desc: The sponsor takes back up to the pool's unlocked balance and unused credit.

methods.name: openSponsored
methods.desc:
The pool's allocator opens a ticket for `member`, paid from the pool, within the member's use for
this period. Akita's backend uses this for members' routines and triggers. Returns the ticket id.

args.name: request
args.desc: The caller's id for the request, so the provider can match the ticket to what it served.

methods.name: openGated
methods.desc:
A member who passes the pool's gate opens a ticket for themselves, paid from the pool. `gateTxn`
is the Akita gate's `mustCheck` for the sender and the pool's gate, earlier in the group.

args.name: request
args.desc: The caller's id for the request, so the provider can match the ticket to what it served.

methods.name: settle
methods.desc:
The provider's claim account settles a ticket at the request's actual `cost`, at most what was
locked: the cost less the DAO fee (taken at the rate when the ticket opened) goes to the provider,
and the rest of the lock and the storage deposit go back to the payer. Returns what the provider got.

methods.name: refundExpired
methods.desc: After a ticket's settle window, anyone may return the whole lock and the storage deposit to the payer.

methods.name: poolRemaining
methods.desc: What `member` has left in `pool` this period.

methods.name: providerCost
methods.desc: What `registerProvider` charges for storage with this metadata URI.

desc:
Akita's inference network: a registry of inference providers, and the ledger of what wallets pay them.

Providers register with an AKTA bond of at least the DAO's `providerBond` and, while registration is
closed, wait as Pending until the admin activates them. A provider's box names its owner, the claim
account that settles its tickets, and the payout address. The metadata box holds a URI for its models and
prices, and the attestation box is where a provider running in a TEE publishes its measurement and
encryption key, for private inference later.

Members pay per request, straight from their wallets, the way ZeroSignal's escrow works. For each
request the caller (the member's app, or the key that runs their routines and triggers) opens a
ticket through InferencePlugin that locks the request's max price from the member's spending account.
The provider serves at once, without waiting for the ticket to confirm, then settles it at the actual
cost: the provider gets the cost less the DAO's `chargePercentage`, and the rest comes back to the
member. A ticket left unsettled past the settle window is refunded in full. A provider whose ticket
never lands cuts the member off, losing at most that request.

A sponsor (such as Akita, for usage included with a subscription) can fund a pool instead. A member
who passes the pool's gate, or the pool's allocator on a member's behalf, opens tickets paid from the
pool, up to the pool's amount per member per period; what a ticket does not spend goes back to the
pool and to the member's allowance.

The provider never opens tickets and can never take more than a ticket locked. A provider that
settles for usage it did not serve is paused, its bond slashed to whoever the admin names (such as
the members it overcharged), and it is banned.

admin.desc: Sets the network's settings, payment assets and provider status, and slashes. Meant to be the DAO wallet.

version.desc: the current version of the contract

akitaDAO.desc: the app ID of the Akita DAO
